expansion_factor_measured: 4.3x (tachyzoites, standard U-ExM); 2.5x (bradyzoites, standard U-ExM); 4.2x (D7 bradyzoites in HFFs, StcE–U-ExM)
extraction_notes: Novel StcE mucinase pre-treatment step added before anchoring to enable full cyst expansion. Two NHS ester catalogue numbers listed (72464, 08741) for Atto 565 and 594 respectively. Standard (non-ExM) IFA also performed; SAG1 Ab used only in std IFA.

extraction_notes: Cryo-fixation uses liquid ethane plunge-freezing then freeze-substitution in acetone+0.1%PFA+0.02%GA overnight on dry ice. title: Diatom ultrastructural diversity across controlled and natural environments
fixation_reagent: plunge freezing (liquid ethane or ethane-propane), freeze substitution in acetone with formaldehyde and glutaraldehyde
expansion_factor_measured: inferred: ~5.3x (biological scale 9.45 µm / expanded scale 50 µm)
extraction_notes: cryo-ExM protocol: plunge-freeze then freeze-substitute in acetone+0.5%FA+0.025%GA. Supp. Table 1 provides species-specific expansion factors. P. tricornutum showed low EF (1.87x). Secondary Ab catalogue numbers A32727/A11011/A11034/A11001 are listed; the specific pairings per target were inferred from methods. Chaetoceros sp. environmental samples from Tallinn and Plentzia split into one entry.

extraction_notes: This paper primarily describes a metalens (DBBM) for extended depth-of-field imaging. The fixation solution ('cell-fix solution') includes 1% acrylamide as an anchoring agent co-applied with fixatives. extraction_notes: 1. This paper primarily develops the CATS (Comprehensive Analysis of Tissues across Scales) method, which integrates STED microscopy and expansion microscopy. ExM is used as one component of the platform rather than being the sole focus. 2. The human hippocampal tissue (surgery specimen) is used at confocal resolution with rCATS but it is not explicitly expanded — expansion not confirmed for this specimen in the main text. 6. Antibody supplier/clone information is not provided in the main text; full Methods details may be in supplementary material not included. 7. The coCATS STED experiments (without expansion) are also a major part of the paper and involve mouse brain tissue; these are included as the ExM-relevant entries. 8. Human organoid experiment uses STED (z-STED) but ExM application is not explicitly stated for organoids — labelled as pre-expansion since it is part of the CATS platform discussion. anchoring_reagent: biotinylated WGA transferred to acrylamide-modified streptavidin (rCATS)
extraction_notes: 1. This paper primarily develops the CATS (Comprehensive Analysis of Tissues across Scales) method, which integrates STED microscopy and expansion microscopy. ExM is used as one component of the platform rather than being the sole focus. 2. Two ExM approaches are used: MAP (ref 6, Ku et al. 2016) and protein-retention ExM (ref 8, Tillberg et al. 2016) — classified as 'other: MAP / proExM' since both variants are employed. 3. Detailed gel composition (sodium acrylate %, acrylamide %, bis-acrylamide %) are not specified in the main text; protocol details reference published MAP and proExM methods. 4. The organotypic slice experiments use coCATS (NHS-PEG12-biotin) with heat/SDS denaturation (MAP approach) or enzymatic digestion (proExM approach) — ~4x expansion. Fixed adult mouse sections use rCATS (biotinylated WGA + acrylamide-modified streptavidin) with ~4–4.5x expansion by protein-retention ExM. 5. The human hippocampal tissue (surgery specimen) is used at confocal resolution with rCATS but it is not explicitly expanded — expansion not confirmed for this specimen in the main text. 6. Antibody supplier/clone information is not provided in the main text; full Methods details may be in supplementary material not included. 7. The coCATS STED experiments (without expansion) are also a major part of the paper and involve mouse brain tissue; these are included as the ExM-relevant entries. 8. Human organoid experiment uses STED (z-STED) but ExM application is not explicitly stated for organoids — labelled as pre-expansion since it is part of the CATS platform discussion.
